conventions.convention: An RCBD has integer t ≥ 2 and b ≥ 1, assignment space (S_t)^b, and uniform independent within-block permutations. Assignment randomness supplies no response model or no-interference assumption.

Paired outcomes are fixed real own-treatment potential outcomes with no interference; treatment 1 is assigned to exactly one unit uniformly. D is treated minus control, and design moments hold the schedule fixed.
S is the latent unit-level effect of the selected treated unit, rather than the observed paired contrast; no single observed-data statistic represents it over the unrestricted schedule model.
Cell arrays use treatment index i and block index j, the Frobenius inner product, zero-sum treatment and block effects, and a full-row-rank contrast matrix C satisfying C1_t = 0.

The exact F law assumes AC and, conditional on the realized assignment, additive means and independent N(0, σ²) errors with σ² > 0. Both degrees are positive, and the statistic is zero when RSS_U = 0.
Latin-square randomization is uniform over all Latin-square allocations on residues 0 through t−1, including order one; it is not merely random relabeling of one selected square.

load_bearing.statement: For t,b ≥ 2 and full-row-rank C with 1 ≤ q ≤ t−1 and C1_t = 0, dim W_U = t+b−1, dim W_R(C) = t+b−1−q, W_U⊥ is the double-centered residual space E of dimension (t−1)(b−1), RSS_U is the squared norm of the double-centered array, and RSS_R−RSS_U = b(Cȳ)ᵀ(CCᵀ)⁻¹(Cȳ).

The randomized complete-block design uses assignment space (S_t)^b and the uniform probability law on this finite nonempty set. Each assignment has probability (t!)^(−b); within-block treatment permutations are independent and individually uniform.
For fixed no-interference potential outcomes in a uniformly randomized pair, E_d[D] = τ and Var_d(D) = (D_1−D_2)²/4 = ((δ_1−δ_2)+2(Y_1(0)−Y_2(0)))²/4.

For the fixed treatment effect S of whichever unit receives treatment 1 in paired randomization, E_d[S] = τ and Var_d(S) = (δ_1−δ_2)²/4. S uses both potential outcomes of the selected unit and is not a statistic of the observed assignment and response data.

With one observation per treatment-block cell and unrestricted double-centered interaction γ, the additive-fit residual is γ+P_Eε and also equals (γ+h)+(P_Eε−h) for every h ∈ E. Fitting unrestricted interaction leaves zero pure-error residual degrees of freedom; this is an algebraic limitation, not universal stochastic nonidentifiability.
A Latin-square allocation uses each treatment exactly once in every row and every column. The specified randomization law is uniform on the finite nonempty set of all such allocations.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 defines D to be zero on the zero-weight assignments (0,0) and (1,1). Proof 2.3 then states “D=D_2+(D_1-D_2)X”, where X indicates that unit 1 receives treatment 1. This identity need not hold on those two assignments with the chosen extension. It holds almost surely on the positive-weight support, which suffices for the variance argument, but that qualification is missing.

seams_checked.note: Checked the assignment-model and finite-population-target definitions against the batch's uses. Fixed schedules, assignment-only randomness, and permitted zero-weight assignments are preserved. The paired theorem explicitly embeds the restricted design in the supplier's full binary assignment space with zero weights elsewhere and adds no interference separately. The Gaussian theorem explicitly adds its error model. The supplier page's distinction between design-based inference and Gaussian response assumptions agrees with the consumer page; no reverse dependency or stronger sharp-null claim is asserted.
